sectors.name: Technology
themes: Indonesia's tech sector is decoupling from US semis, driven by domestic liquidity and retail participation favoring small-cap names like SLIS and SNDK.
Global AI infrastructure spending continues to funnel into storage and equipment makers (WDC, AMAT, TER), creating durable earnings tailwinds for US-listed suppliers.
Local currency stability and government digitalization initiatives underpin sustained demand for Indonesian tech listings, reducing beta to US rate cycles.
sectors.ai: Buy the Indonesia tech complex on relative strength: SLIS, SNDK, and WGSH lead with double-digit momentum while US semis lag, signaling local capital rotation into domestic names. Add exposure to storage and semiconductor equipment proxies (WDC, AMAT, TER) as AI-driven demand persists, but trim into any 5%+ single-day spikes to lock gains.

themes: Indonesian microfinance and rural lenders are outperforming on domestic credit demand, a structural tailwind from rising consumption and SME formalization.
US financial weakness is a decoupling opportunity—local banks with strong NIMs and low dollar exposure will keep re-rating as IDR stability holds.
Consolidation in the insurance sector (TUGU, PEGE) is driving revaluation, with M&A premiums and capital optimization as durable value drivers.
sectors.ai: Buy selective Indonesian financials on idiosyncratic strength—STAR (+22%) and XCIS (+10%) signal local credit/microfinance momentum, while US drag is transient. Favor AHAP, ASMI, and DNAR for continued upside; avoid broad beta, rotate into niche lenders with earnings catalysts.

sectors.ai: Buy dips in Indonesia-listed renewables names, especially VKTR and TOBA, as local momentum (+0.32%) diverges from US weakness (-1.15%)—a signal of domestic policy-driven demand. Rotate out of US-exposed climate tech into IDX green leaders ahead of Q3 earnings, targeting PGEO and ARKO for 10-15% upside.

sectors.name: Infrastructure
themes: Domestic toll road and port operators are outperforming as Indonesia's logistics corridor expansion accelerates, driven by new capital projects and rising inter-island trade volumes.
Digital infrastructure names like LINK and EXCL benefit from structural data center and 5G rollout demand, with tower leasing rates and fiber penetration still below regional peers.
US-linked infrastructure plays face headwinds from higher-for-longer rates, making local-currency, government-backed projects the preferred risk-adjusted exposure.
sectors.ai: Buy pullbacks in TEBE and YPAS after their limit-up moves, as both signal sustained domestic momentum in toll and port logistics. Rotate out of US-exposed names like PACK and ASLI, which lag on Fed uncertainty. Favor LINK for digital infrastructure upside, and accumulate EXCL on telecom tower re-rating.

sectors.ai: Buy selective Indonesian healthcare names with domestic revenue exposure, as the sector's +0.34% ID outperformance versus US -0.27% confirms local resilience. SRAJ (+15.38%) and PEHA (+13.64%) signal momentum in pharma distribution and hospital supplies; add on pullbacks, but avoid US-linked laggards. Position for Q3 earnings catalysts, prioritizing firms with pricing power and government procurement ties.

sectors.name: Logistics
themes: Indonesia's port and toll-road infrastructure upgrades are structurally lowering logistics costs, benefiting domestic operators like TAXI and HATM over foreign peers.
Cold-chain and temperature-controlled logistics demand is rising with the expansion of Indonesia's pharmaceutical and FMCG sectors, underpinning ASSA's durable growth.
Air cargo capacity constraints and e-commerce cross-border flows are creating recurring rate tailwinds for GIAA and SHIP, though these are more volatile than land-based logistics.
sectors.ai: Buy TAXI and HATM on continued domestic logistics consolidation and port efficiency gains; GIAA upside is freight-rate driven but air cargo exposure is cyclical, so take partial profits. Maintain overweight on ASSA for resilient cold-chain demand. Trim US-linked names (AMKBY, CBRE) as ID outperformance persists.
